designAnswers.inboxAppendAndHook: The same injected hook. appendCampaignCombatOutcomeBatch gains an optional afterCommit (CampaignCommandCommitHook) that runs on the extension's handle after the receipt insert, in the committed arm only, inside the one immediate transaction; the store's appendCombatOutcomeBatch passes this.rewriteRecordAfterCommand, which bindJournalCapabilityPorts installs on the co-op host's store, as appendCommandBatch does (:443). The constant line of JournalCampaignEventStore.ts is not touched.
designAnswers.rosterMapping: rewriteCampaignRecordAfterCommand also patches body.rosterProjection.units[].readiness from the journal's rosterUnits status for every unit present in both (operational -> Ready, damaged -> Damaged, destroyed -> Destroyed; the inverse of campaignSourceGenesis.ts:51-55). Force membership is unchanged: a destroyed unit stays in the journal and in its force, so projectForceUnits never meets an absent unit. A journal unit absent from the projection (a recoveredUnit without a unitRef) is not written; a record without a roster projection has no readiness to patch. Since the rewrite is shared, a command batch's rewrite patches readiness too (a no-op unless the journal's roster status changed).
designAnswers.destroyedChangeKind: 'repaired' carrying status destroyed (accepted by the schema pack, attempt 1 p3), at CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:190 and reconcileCoopBattle.ts:226. Design risk to measure in red/local: the reducer replaces the unit with payload.unit (applyCampaignEvent.ts:53-56), whose {unitId, designation, status} carries no unitRef or unitSource, while a checkpoint re-projects them from the record (campaignSourceGenesis.ts:114-123); the live host and the journal would then differ after the host's save (row o1's agreement check). If measured, the derivation carries the unit's own ledger fields forward and changes only its status, in the same line region of the files already named.
designAnswers.duplicateReceipt: The inbox's receipt lookup inside the transaction (campaignCombatOutcomeInbox.ts:81-101) answers a duplicate or a version conflict before append(); the hook runs only after the receipt insert in the committed arm, so it runs once per outcome id (row i; mutant M3).
designAnswers.stalePutAfterOutcome: The outcome's rewrite advances the record's version, so a host save built at the pre-outcome version answers 409 with the rewritten record ([id].ts:228-255); the host adopts it through U35f's refresh when it folds the outcome's frames (CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:120 publishes them). o2u is re-measured in red and local.
designAnswers.authorityGate: Unchanged from U35e: the rewrite reads the cutover marker on the writer handle and writes nothing unless it is in journal state (campaignRecordJournalState.ts:79-80); row a and mutant M5.

hostSaveModelForRows: The host's whole-campaign save after an outcome is modelled as U35e's c1 row: a PUT of the host's envelope at the version the host held before the outcome (the host fold of the live host state onto the campaign it held, or the held campaign unfolded for o2u), then a GET and a PUT of the server record at its own version (the host taking the server record after a 409, as U35f's refresh does). On the baseline the first PUT is accepted.

risksForTheParent: Authority: on a journal-native campaign every first-receipt combat outcome writes the saved record (version + 1, the journal's balance, date and roster readiness), so a host save built before the outcome answers 409 with the server record; the host adopts it through U35f's refresh.
Idempotency: the rewrite runs only in the inbox's committed arm; a duplicate or an outcome-version conflict rewrites nothing (row i, M3).
Concurrency: the rewrite runs on the extension's handle inside the outcome's immediate transaction (row t, M2); a whole-campaign PUT is ordered wholly before or after the outcome.

Migration: none under OD-mvp-hard-cutover; the rewrite spreads the raw stored JSON without the read migration ladder, as U35e's does. Lane B: the owner's ruling on the head that merges (authority, idempotency, concurrency, migration).

Visible change: a destroyed unit is no longer deleted from the journal; it stays in the host state and every mirror with status destroyed (the guest's roster count includes it: FN-u35g-kept-destroyed-units-in-guest-roster-count), and the feed reads '<designation> destroyed'.
Shared rewrite: command batches run the same rewrite, which now also patches roster readiness from the journal on a journal-native campaign.
